subject: vignette build error only occurs when building package

messages.author: 4184023bb084c468
messages.subject: vignette build error only occurs when building package
parts:
Hi,

I've made some changes to the RGalaxy package which has a knitr .Rmd vignette.

Now when I try and build the package with R CMD build, I get this:

[...]
* creating vignettes ... ERROR
Quitting from lines 234-235 (RGalaxy-vignette.Rmd) 
Error: processing vignette 'RGalaxy-vignette.Rmd' failed with diagnostics:
missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
Execution halted

I can't reproduce this error when I do any of the following:

knit("RGalaxy-vignette.Rmd")
knit2html("RGalaxy-vignette.Rmd")
purl("RGalaxy-vignette.Rmd")
source("RGalaxy-vignette.R", echo=TRUE, max=Inf())

The line numbers 234-235 are helpful but the fact that I can't reproduce this interactively means I can't use any interactive tools (debug(), traceback(), etc) to better find the error.

So why is the vignette failing to build during R CMD build but not giving an error with knit()?

Thanks,
Dan

parts: I just had such a problem about 10 minutes ago!  Get rid of all the files in the vignette folder but the .Rnw, .bib, .cls  The versions I had created when knitting directly polluted the build process with all the intermediate files that get created, which upset build I guess.  Bryan

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] vignette build error only occurs when building package
parts:
I'm not quite sure what was the problem, but one major difference
between running knit() alone and compiling the vignettes using knitr
is that knitr will stop on errors in code chunks in the latter case,
and will not in the former case. That is because I set
opts_knit$set(stop_on_error = 2) before compiling package vignettes,
which can be helpful to prevent unexpected errors.

This is a decision that I find hard to make -- whether to stop on
error or not. By default, knitr does not stop, just like you paste the
code into R console, but this may not be a good choice because people
may not even notice the errors if knitr did not stop.

Regards,
Yihui
